ideas: Install it as a Claude Code plugin (/plugin install android-skills --marketplace android/skills) or through Codex's plugin marketplace, then ask the agent to make one of your apps edge-to-edge and see how the edge-to-edge skill shapes the change.
Run migrate-xml-views-to-jetpack-compose on one legacy XML screen from a past client app and compare the result with an unassisted agent run.
Let an agent do an AGP 9 or Play Billing Library upgrade on a branch with the agp-9-upgrade and play-billing-library-version-upgrade skills, and review the diff.
Use r8-analyzer and android-profiler to have an agent explain your release build's shrinker keep-rules and a performance trace.
Prototype an on-device AI feature with the device-ai skills (ml-kit-genai-prompt-api, litert-runtime) or expose app actions to agents with appfunctions.

featured.reason: Desktop orchestrator that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents side by side in isolated git worktrees, with Design Mode (click a UI element to send its HTML/CSS and a screenshot to the agent), diff annotation, SSH worktrees, a scriptable CLI and an iOS/Android companion. Large Electron + Expo codebase; use the signed release builds.
ideas: Give the same feature prompt to Claude Code and Codex in separate Orca worktrees, comment on both diffs with Annotate AI Diffs, and merge the better one.
Open ai-daily-radar in Design Mode and click a card to send its HTML, CSS and a cropped screenshot straight into the agent's prompt for UI polish.
Pair the Android companion APK so you get a notification when a long agent run finishes and can send follow-ups from your phone.
Script a repeatable check with the Orca CLI (orca worktree create, snapshot, click, fill), for example a page smoke test after every agent change.
Study its Expo/React Native mobile app and the orca-emulator-android skill to learn how an agent drives an adb emulator (taps, logcat, accessibility tree) for mobile QA.

featured.reason: Shared long-term memory and typed handoffs across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and 20+ other harnesses via MCP and lifecycle hooks; plain-markdown, git-backed wiki with a zero-LLM default path. You run its server, and its hooks capture sanitized prompts and tool calls, so review the privacy settings first.
ideas: Quit a Claude Code session mid-task, start ai-memory run codex in the same repo, and check whether the handoff carries the open questions and failed approaches.
Host the memory server on the Mac mini so agent sessions on both the Mac mini and the MacBook Pro share one project memory.
Open its git-backed markdown wiki in Obsidian (or just grep it) to audit and hand-edit what your agents remember about a project.
Turn on the cross-project profile so your usual stack (package manager, test layout, Android and web conventions) reaches every new repo at session start.
Read docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the memory-aging design to learn how zero-LLM decay, dedup and contradiction flags work before adding memory to your own agent tools.
